quoted.text:
Ate at Benihana on weekend. Been reading up on it and super interesting. Does 20%+ operating margins. Great for restaurants. 

Harvard Business School even did a case study on benefits of hibachi/teppanyaki model:

▫️MAXIMIZE REAL ESTATE: Back kitchen area mostly for prep. Leaves more space for seating in dining area. Grill tables standardized to seat 8.  Don’t have to deal with a bunch of different seating set ups.

▫️EFFICIENT TABLE SERVICE: Table service typically begins once 8 people seated. Chefs master the same sequence: rice, vegetables, protein, jokes (and that glorious volcano onion). Less chance of mistakes and table times predictable. 

When chef is done, leaves grill table, a subtle hint for guests to leave (and turn the table for more customers).

A table having to wait to seat 8 before cooking does introduce inefficiencies, though…but, during this time, customers usually asked to hang out at the bar (which sells high margin sushi and drinks).

▫️MENU SIMPLIFICATION: Majority of grill menu is three proteins (chicken, steak, shrimp), vegetables (zucchini, onions), rice and sauces. 

The menu mixes and matches options (I had Rocky’s favourite: steak & chicken) to look like variety, but it’s really only handful of ingredients.

Benihana can buy these ingredients in bulk to save. There’s less wasted food and easier for chef to memorize/master cooking (straightforwardness of menu also makes it easier for chef to entertain — eg. egg shell in hat — and drop them jokes).

posts.text:
TWELVE HOURS IN THE JENSEN HUANG CASE FROM 10PM TO 10AM on 11/15/26

In this window the channel record widened again: the Wall Street Journal reported records showing Megaspeed arranged to send nearly $12 billion of top Nvidia chips to companies in China, a fifth chip figure with its own window, and reported an unwritten Nvidia rule capping partners' Chinese customers and a new channel node, Aolani Cloud. Megaspeed answered publicly for the first time on Alice Huang, saying she left the company effective August 30, 2025 and that it has retained outside counsel for an internal investigation. The Washington Post reported Huang is quietly helping pick his own successor, and Elon Musk said many of Nvidia's supply deals were a handshake with Huang personally.

A FIFTH CHIP FIGURE

• The Wall Street Journal reported that records it reviewed show Megaspeed arranged to send nearly $12 billion worth of top-of-the-line Nvidia chips to companies in China between March 2024 and June 2025, the shipment records showing orders for several hundred thousand chips. The records do not show how much of the hardware was actually delivered or where it originated.
• This is a fifth chip figure in the case, owned by the Journal with its own window. It is not merged or summed with the other four: the customs figure of at least $4.6 billion and at least 136,000 GPUs from 2023 to November 2025, the Speedmatrix reconstruction of $4.606 billion from December 2024 to January 2026, the $4.8 billion figure from June 2024 to February 2026, or the network figure of at least $7.5 billion and about 240,000 chips since 2023. The Journal's reporting rests on records it reviewed; the records themselves were not seen in the case record.

THE RULES NVIDIA SET, UNWRITTEN

• The Journal also reported that beginning last year Nvidia required many of its cloud partners outside China to keep their Chinese customers below a certain level, which has shifted between 30% and 49%, though the rule was not written into any contracts, people familiar with the matter said.
• Per the same reporting, Nvidia also urged some cloud partners to weed out Chinese nationals from top management and push out Chinese investors, the people said.

A NEW CHANNEL NODE

• The Journal reported that Aolani Cloud, a Singapore cloud-computing provider and Nvidia partner, courted investors last year saying the geopolitical situation provided a unique opportunity for companies that could connect Chinese customers with advanced chips, explaining in an investor presentation viewed by the Journal that top Chinese internet companies had to rent the chips they were blocked from buying.
• Per the Journal, Aolani's investors helped it fund some $2.5 billion in hardware in Malaysia by the beginning of this year, and its anchor customer is ByteDance. Aolani says it has systems in place to strictly adhere to U.S. regulations and has been focused on building a global customer base.

MEGASPEED ANSWERS

• Megaspeed told CNBC on Sunday, November 15, in an emailed statement: "Ms. Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed effective August 30, 2025 and currently has no role with the Company," adding "Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang's personal and private matters." The August 30, 2025 date places her exit before the affair reporting broke in late October 2026.
• In the same statement, Megaspeed said media reports about its business, supply chain and global operations are not supported by verifiable evidence and that it has retained external legal counsel, no firm named, to conduct a "thorough internal investigation". It stated that it "designs and maintains its global operational and supply-chain control frameworks to comply with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes, including United States export control requirements", and added that it will review the reporting and communicate further with stakeholders as appropriate.
• The Journal separately reported that Megaspeed said this past week that it retained a U.S.

posts.name: Ted Zhang
posts.text:
Paul Tudor Jones: Almost Every Big Crash Has the Same Root Cause, Too Much Leverage Somewhere

If I think of some really, really big accidents, most of them have the same underlying reason, same underlying foundation, which is some too much leverage somewhere. Most of the leverage, most of the time, if I think of the big ones, were derivative inspired, either futures or options.

1987, that crash was 100% portfolio insurance, 100%. Had they had limits, which they didn't, it would have been a 10%, maybe 15% max, but that was 100% derivatives.

If I think about 1998, Long-Term Capital, big derivatives, they had a huge balance sheet with a lot of derivatives they were offsides on.

2000 was a little different. 2000 was the easiest bear market I've ever seen in my whole life. It's got so many similarities to right now in the sense that the bear market of 2001 and 2002 were a consequence of all the IPOs in 99, 2000, and then as they unlocked, you just had this never-ending cascade of selling.

posts.name: InvestmentGuru
posts.text:
Canada’s real estate crisis is real, and the risks could be much bigger than many people are prepared for.

Buyers are disappearing, homes are sitting on the market, affordability remains stretched, and job losses are adding another layer of pressure. Now add the risk of energy-driven inflation pushing interest rates higher or keeping borrowing costs elevated for longer.

This is a dangerous combination. Falling demand, declining purchasing power, mortgage renewals, unemployment and highly leveraged households can create a vicious cycle.

2008 should be a reminder of how quickly confidence can disappear when the housing market turns. Canada may have a different set of underlying problems, but that doesn’t mean the consequences will be any less painful.

The biggest risk isn’t just falling home prices. It’s what happens when people can no longer afford to hold the homes they bought at yesterday’s prices.

The housing market doesn’t need a crash in a single day. It only needs buyers to disappear and forced sellers to show up.

The two numbers that matter this morning.

GDP growth: +1.5% versus +2.1% expected. Down from +2.1% last quarter. The economy is decelerating.

GDP price index: +6.3% versus +3.6% expected. Up from +3.6% last quarter. Inflation is accelerating.

Growth falling while prices rising. That is the definition of stagflation. Not a warning. The data just printed it.

The magnitude of the inflation miss is what matters. The GDP chain price did not come in slightly above expectations. It came in 75% above consensus. 6.3% versus 3.6%. Analysts were modeling a repeat of Q1. They got a near-doubling. This is the largest upside miss on the GDP deflator since the tariff-driven import price shocks began.

Now connect this to yesterday's FOMC. Three members dissented wanting a rate hike. Kashkari's dissent was called a hawkish surprise. This morning's data proves he was right. posts.name: Mark Zandi
posts.text: AI has been a boon to economic growth and job creation, but it's coming with side effects. It’s adding to inflation by driving up electricity and consumer electronics prices, and pushing up interest rates by soaking up capital to finance the AI build-out. It’s also coming at the expense of other investment. Since ChatGPT debuted four years ago, AI has gone from a rounding error to nearly two-thirds of the growth in investment, while growth in everything else has slowed by more than half since mid-2024. The bet on AI had better pay off in higher productivity, because the rest of the economy isn't investing enough to deliver it.
